v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-04). The majority of disputed bills (59%, 1,785 of 3,025, E-01) carry ACTUAL (not estimated) read types, indicating a billing calculation or tariff-application defect in the billing-import step is producing wrong bills on normally-read accounts — independent of any tariff rate change (ruled out, E-02) and independent of response-time capacity (already within SLA, E-03). A separate, smaller mechanism — field manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target (E-05) — plausibly drives estimate substitution for the remaining minority of disputed (ESTIMATED-read) bills.
v2_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month starting August 2026 (E-04). The dominant confirmed mechanism is billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), an unscaled high-consumption check that misclassifies valid AMI reads from v4.2-firmware meters — whose registers report in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy m3 (E-13) — as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution instead of billing from the received read; this explains 1,184 of the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-14, E-15). This same BV-17/firmware-unit mechanism does not extend to the larger population of 1,785 disputed ACTUAL-read bills (59% of all disputed bills, E-01): billing-db's own account-level determination (E-15) shows zero ACTUAL-read accounts in the BV-17/v4.2-affected set, so the majority of disputes has a cause distinct from this confirmed defect and remains unidentified by current evidence.
